chapter: South America and back in New York
title: Madrid, the royal visit, bullfights and Moorish-flavoured music
summary: In Madrid they restart the show for the Spanish royals, learn the anthem, and hear Catalonian music he links to the Moors.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Yes, it was a form of blackmail. But we had to do it. Because we couldn't go on. And then we moved on to Madrid. I know it was the Infanta Beatriz there. And we had played the show halfway through when we had to start it all over again. Because Queen Elizabeth and Ferdinand, they came in the theater. And, first place, we didn't know the Spanish National Anthem, so we had to run around and find somebody to play that for us, see?

But anyhow, we started the show all over and we had a wonderful time there in Madrid. But the thing that was bothering us was, we couldn't stay out late because we didn't understand how to get back in the house. Because they have that custom there, applaud, patting your hands and you don't have no key, and if you pat your hands and you don't have no key, anything can happen to you before you get in. You see?

And also, that was our first chance to see a bullfight. And listen to the music of Catalonia. They had the music, in fact, even the instruments were original. This music was the wildest thing. I think it was part Moorish music. It was the

wildest thing you had ever heard. It was like it was written on a different scale than our scale. The diatonic scale. You see, so. And then we had trouble there. But, outside of that, after we finished there we headed straight back. And on our way we stopped in Vienna and -- but we headed straight for Berlin after that. That's where I left the wife off. And then we went into Russia. I thought we should say that because we had quite some experiences down there in Spain. A little different from the regular -- in fact, could almost be considered not European.

More Asiatic, or African. See, on account of the Moors that were in there for so many years. And they left their stamp there. Until Le Cid kicked them out of there. But that was way up in Ferdinand and Isabella's time. But the Moors had been there ever since Mohammed's day. Ever since 700.
